title: This week's cases
sub: Fake officials, 'scam recovery' ads, card-tap apps and post-breach phishing

ex.q: Tap every red flag in this call

segs.text: Hello, am I speaking to the account holder?
You just bought two iPhones on a new mobile plan.
If it wasn't you, your details were misused. I'll put you through to the police now.
Officer: move your savings to a safe account, or hand cash to our officer for checks.

ex.why: Singapore police reported at least 59 cases in October 2026 where callers posing as SIMBA staff passed victims to fake police or MAS officers. Losses topped $1.3 million. Real officials never transfer your call to the police or ask for money. Hang up and call the company's official number.

ex.q: You lost money to a scam. A Facebook ad shows a police officer offering to 'recover your money'. It asks for your number, then an OTP. What is it?
opts: A real police service, so share the OTP
A scam. Police never advertise scam recovery
Safe if the officer looks real
Fine if the ad has many likes
ex.why: Singapore police warned in Oct 2026 about Facebook ads using AI-made pictures of officers. Sharing the OTP can let scammers into your accounts. Never share an OTP. Report through your official police channel or hotline instead.

ex.q: Match what the fake 'officer' says to the truth
pairs: 'There's a warrant. Pay now or go to jail.'
Police never demand payment by phone
'Pay with gift cards, crypto or gold.'
'Join your court hearing on Zoom now.'
Hang up and call a number you trust
ex.why: Boston police warned in Oct 2026 of a rise in callers posing as police or court staff, including one fake court hearing held over Zoom. Hang up, then call the agency on a number you already know is real.

msg.text: Hi, I paid for your rice cooker already! Here is the Carousell invoice (PDF). To receive the money, scan the QR code or verify your bank at carousell-payout.top/receive

ex.why: Singapore police say fake buyers move chats to WhatsApp or Telegram, then send a fake invoice with a QR code. It leads to a fake bank page that steals your login and OTP. At least 63 cases since July 2026. Only check payments inside the marketplace's official app.

ex.q: Put this card-tap scam from the Netherlands in order
steps: A recorded AI voice warns of odd activity on your account
You press 1 and a fake bank worker comes on the line
They rush you to install a 'bank' app
You hold your bank card against your phone
A helper uses your card data at a cash machine
ex.why: Dutch police arrested two men in Oct 2026 over this trick. About 170 victims lost around €380,000 in three weeks. No bank asks you to tap your card on your phone. Hang up and call the number printed on your card.

ex.q: Japan Airlines said in Oct 2026 that hackers reached some customers' booking data through a supplier. If you were affected, what should you watch for next?
opts: Phishing emails and calls pretending to be the airline
A refund that arrives by itself
ex.why: About 92,000 customers were affected, and JAL warned them about phishing emails, fake calls and look-alike websites. Scammers use leaked details to sound real. Go to the company's official app or website yourself.

ex.q: A caller says you won a charity sweepstakes because you donated. You just need to pay a small fee to claim it. What do you do?
opts: Give your ID number instead of paying
Hang up. Real prizes are free
Ask them to call back tomorrow
ex.why: The US FTC warned in Oct 2026 about scammers posing as well-known charities. If you must pay or give your ID number to get a prize, it's a scam. Caller ID can be faked, so look up the charity yourself.
